passage:
Urmila had chosen the venue for the college fest talk: the open-air court by the canteen. Everyone nodded. Dhruv thought it was a bold idea, and he wanted the fest to go well. But he had seen dark clouds all week. He put his hand up. “Urmila, I'm with you on the open-air court, and I'll set it all up. But if it rains on Saturday we have no backup, and two hundred people will be standing in it. Can we book the seminar hall as plan B?”

Urmila paused. “Book it.”

Dhruv sent the request that afternoon. On Saturday it rained at noon, and the seminar hall was ready. Urmila only said, “Thanks for saying it.”

qa.q: Where had Urmila chosen to hold the fest talk?
qa.a: Urmila had chosen the open-air court by the canteen.

qa.q: What was Dhruv thinking when he put his hand up?
qa.a: Dhruv liked the bold idea and wanted the fest to succeed, but worried because of the dark clouds and the lack of a backup.

qa.q: What choice did Dhruv make that helped the fest?
qa.a: Dhruv backed the open-air plan but plainly asked for the seminar hall as plan B, and booked it that afternoon.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt when Dhruv raised the risk in front of everyone?
qa.a: Urmila may have felt a flash of defensiveness at a plan being questioned, but was willing to listen since Dhruv backed the direction.

grounding: A team member supports the group's direction but says plainly when a problem is visible, showing loyalty and honesty together.

“So the plan is, we finish the entire prototype by Wednesday,” Payal said, looking around the lab table.

“I'm in,” said Kashish. “I'll take the casing. But Payal, one thing. The battery we ordered won't fit the casing. I checked twice.”

“It fits in the drawing.”

“The drawing has the old measurements. If we go ahead, we'll waste two days.”

Nikhil grimaced. “Or we just make the casing bigger.”

“Yes,” Payal said, half laughing, half sighing. “Fine. Kashish, thanks for saying it now and not on Wednesday.”

“I want it to work,” said Kashish. “I'm with you all the way to Wednesday.”

Payal pulled the drawing across the table and started crossing out the old numbers.

qa.q: By when did Payal want the prototype finished?
qa.a: Payal wanted the entire prototype finished by Wednesday.

qa.q: What did Kashish want when raising the battery problem?
qa.a: Kashish was worried the prototype would fail and wanted to save the two days that going ahead with old measurements would waste, while staying with the plan.

qa.q: What choice did Kashish make that Payal was thankful for?
qa.a: Kashish agreed to the plan but plainly said the battery would not fit, and said it before Wednesday.

qa.q: How might Payal have felt when Kashish challenged the drawing?
qa.a: Payal was probably irritated for a moment, but relieved to learn of the problem early, as the half-laughing sigh suggests.

grounding: A team member supports the group's direction but says plainly when a problem is visible, showing loyalty and honesty together.
